doc.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Joe Williams as master blues singer
summary: Brown praises Joe Williams as a true blues singer who has not compromised his style.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Have you had an opportunity to either sing on the same program with or privy to the personal sounds of Joe Williams?

Well of course. Joe was in the band when we was touring together. And of course we now live in the same town, in Vegas. Joe’s been living there quite a while. In fact the last time I saw him we did the tribute for Peggy Lee. And Joe, again, is like what I call the master blues singer. He is the master. The most, not predictable, but really predictable. You almost know where he’s going musically you know. And I think one of the greater voices that I’ve ever heard is Joe Williams. And he still remains that way. Very proud to that effect. He doesn’t — how should I say — he has not prostituted that particular sound that he has, that style that he has. He’s just true blues singer. “Every Day I Have the Blues” is his. Who else does it, you know what I’m saying? And, “Going to Chicago sorry I can’t take you” — you understand — “Ain’t nothin’ in Chicago that a monkey person can do.” That belongs to Joe Williams. Yes, I know him very well and proud to say I know him.
